entries.question_prompt: Q1. Which combination indicates that car K starts southeast of car L’s destination?
entries.independent_reasoning: In i, B%L places L’s destination at A. K&A means K turns right and reaches A, so K starts at C. C (east) is southeast of A (north).

entries.question_prompt: Q2. Which expressions indicate that car J started at C and reached A? (a) D@J + A; (b) C#J@A; (c) C%J#A.
entries.independent_reasoning: Applying the operator definitions in order, (a) is the only expression that establishes both endpoints C and A; (b) and (c) do not.

entries.question_prompt: Q3. Given B%E + D@F, in which direction is F’s starting point from B, and in which direction is E’s destination from F’s starting point, respectively?
entries.independent_reasoning: B%E puts E’s destination at A (north); D@F puts F’s start at C (east). C is east of B and southeast of A, so the ordered pair is east, southeast.
